en: The Apadāna of the Elder Punnāgapupphiya Gandhodaka Chapter, Number 3 I offered a *punnāga* flower to the Buddha Vipassī, who was seated upon his throne. Because of that deed, I have attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpatti-phala*). May I never again fall into the states of woe. May I never again be born as a woman. May I never again be born in the animal realm. May I never again be born in the world of Yama. May I never again be born among the *asura*s. May I never again be born in the border regions. May I never again be born into a low family. May I never again be dull-witted. May I never again be afflicted by illness. May I never again be short-lived. May I never again be poor. May I never again be ugly. May I never again be one who lacks faith. May I never again be stingy. May I never again be of evil conduct. May I never again be of wrong view. “Having entered the forest grove,
I dwell there as a hunter;
having seen a blossoming *punnāga* tree, I thought:”
I recollected the Best of Buddhas.
Having plucked that fragrant, scented, and beautiful flower, I offered it.
Having built a stupa on the sand,
I offered it to the Buddha.
Ninety-two aeons ago from now,
The flower that I offered in worship—
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
In one ninety-fold aeon,
I was once a dispeller of darkness,
endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Puṇṇāgapupphiya recited these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Puṇṇāgapupphiya.
